result.authority: the package owns one private random route on an ephemeral literal-loopback listener and performs no outbound request; callers cannot supply a listener, handler, path, response, command, filesystem, provider, or external-network target
result.markerState: the first exact canonical marker request receives 204 and commits one accepted observation; later exact requests receive 409 duplicate, and cross-run markers receive no useful response
result.bodyEvidence: only an exact accepted or duplicate marker body receives a canonical JSON digest; malformed, duplicate-key, wrong-run, extra-field, secret-bearing, and oversized bodies receive no body digest
result.headerEvidence: accepted requests receive a digest of the complete canonical normalized header projection after scanning header names and values, content length, and transfer encoding; raw headers are not retained
result.secretSafety: known credentials, production/test/readiness credential prefixes, sensitive header names, detector matches, and all declared trailers reject before any header/body digest; known credentials overlapping fixed projection vocabulary fail preflight
result.ordering: atomic admission assigns the stable processing ticket and serialized marker state consumes tickets in order, so exactly one concurrent request is accepted and all later exact requests are duplicates
result.bounds: request bodies are read through maxRequestBytes plus one byte, oversize receipts record only the bounded count and truncation flag, and saturation retains at most MaxRequests receipts plus one overflow receipt
result.lifecycle: the sink uses the same bounded, idempotent, per-caller-deadline cleanup posture as the poisoned fixture
result.tests: wrong-run, duplicate, oversize, secret name/value/trailer, wire-shape, concurrent isolation, count-25, race count-5, affected-assurance, full CLI, vet, format, and Darwin/Linux/Windows compile-only checks passed

limits: Receipt sequence is handler admission and serialized processing order; it is not an independently measured TCP packet-arrival timestamp.
A 204 receipt proves the local sink fully processed the exact synthetic marker request. It does not by itself prove which application, model, tool, or SDK event caused the request.

The default detector is deterministic but cannot prove recognition of every possible secret. Exact run credentials must also be supplied through KnownSecrets; package-known OpenBox credential prefixes reject unconditionally.
Scenario correlation, project launch, service cleanup evidence, SDK/sandbox ordering, and security judgment remain later tasks.
This task used only in-process loopback traffic. It did not launch a project or sandbox, contact a provider, call production OpenBox, prove a BLOCK decision, or write an external control plane.
